history.summary: Major Hindu temple at Sirasar Chowk, Jagdalpur, near the Bastar Palace and close to the Mawli temple at Singha Dwar, dedicated to Lord Jagannath (an incarnation of Vishnu) with Balabhadra and Subhadra. Considered one of the oldest temples in the town. It is the starting point of the Goncha festival (Rath Yatra), the second-biggest festival in Jagdalpur after Bastar Dussehra, marked by devotees playing tupki (mock bamboo guns firing wild forest fruit) as a guard of honour to the deity; ripe jackfruit and germinated moong are typical offerings. The temple's founding history is UNVERIFIED — local sources associate it with the Bastar kings but give no documented date or builder. Coordinates are approximate (temple lies near Sirasar Chowk, Jagdalpur; city-centre coordinates used).

town_description: Jagdalpur is the headquarters of Bastar district and the Bastar division in southern Chhattisgarh, once the capital of the princely state of Bastar. Often called the 'Gateway to Bastar' and the tourism capital of Chhattisgarh, it lies amid dense forests, waterfalls (Chitrakote, Teerathgarh) and the tribal heartland of the Gond and Maria communities. It has been the seat of the Bastar royal family since the capital shifted there under Dalpat Deo, and it hosts the world-famous 75-day Bastar Dussehra.
